rows.name: DEPLOY_REPO_URL
rows.read_by: `bin/ci/deploy-gh-pages.sh`
rows.values: Git URL of the repository. The script gives the text to `git clone` unchanged. The workflows write `https://x-access-token:<token>@github.com/<repository>.git`.
rows.default: Unset: the script prints `DEPLOY_REPO_URL environment variable must be set` and exits with status 1. An empty value does the same.
rows.effect: The script clones the `gh-pages` branch from this URL. It replaces one directory of the branch with the given report directory. It writes a new `index.html`. It commits and pushes the result.
rows.notes: The workflows put the GitHub token of the run into the URL.

rows.name: DISPATCH_CHANNEL
rows.read_by: `bin/ci/resolve-apt-channel.sh`
rows.values: `unstable` or `testing`, the choices of the workflow input `channel`. Other text that is not empty stops a manual run with `Unknown apt channel`.
rows.default: Unset: no channel is requested. A tag ref selects `testing`. Every other ref selects `unstable`. An empty value does the same.
rows.effect: The script uses the value only when `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` is `workflow_dispatch` (a manual run). The value then selects the APT channel (a package set of the Positron APT server) for the `tron` package.
rows.notes: `testing` is refused when the ref is neither a tag nor a feature branch (a branch other than `main` and `release-*`). A feature branch also needs `FEATURE_TESTING_PUBLISH` set to `1`. The input default is `unstable`.

evidence.quote: printf 'Unknown apt channel %q: expected unstable or testing.\n' \

rows.name: DRY_RUN
rows.read_by: Steps of the jobs `plan` and `refresh` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`). They pass it to `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` as an argument.
rows.values: `true` or `false`. The workflow takes it from the manual run input `dry_run`. Other text stops `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` with `invalid dry-run state`.
rows.default: Unset: does not occur. Both jobs define it. A scheduled run gets `false`. The input default of a manual run is `true`.
rows.effect: `true` marks a dry run of the cost data refresh (the workflow that measures Slice test times again). The job `refresh` skips the default branch checkout. It uses `config/test-benchmarks.json` of the measured commit as base.
rows.notes: A manual run on a branch other than the default branch fails unless the value is `true`. The job `publish` opens the pull request. That job tests the input `dry_run` directly, not this variable. A dry run also writes a note to the step summary.

rows.name: ENABLE_2X72
rows.read_by: Steps of the job `plan` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`). They pass it to `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` as an argument.
rows.values: Text of the repository variable `SLICE_REFRESH_2X72_ENABLED`. Only the exact text `true` enables. All other text counts as not enabled.
rows.default: Unset: the job always defines it. An undefined repository variable gives an empty value. Empty counts as not enabled.
rows.effect: `true` adds the runner class `2x72core` (one kind of benchmark runner) to the cost data refresh (the workflow that measures Slice test times again). Without `true`, a request for `all` refreshes only `2x96core`.
rows.notes: Without `true`, a request for `2x72core` stops the job `plan` with `2x72core refreshes are disabled`. The request is the manual run input `runner_class`. A scheduled run requests `all`.

rows.name: EXPECTED_BITFILE
rows.read_by: The step `Quiesce and run full slice cost-data measurement` of the job `refresh` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`). It passes the value to `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` as an argument.
rows.values: Bitfile identity of the form `<release code>@<year>-<month>-<day>`. The job takes it from the repository variable `SLICE_EXPECTED_BITFILE_2X96CORE` or `SLICE_EXPECTED_BITFILE_2X72CORE`. Letter case is ignored.
rows.default: Unset: the bitfile identity is not compared. An empty value does the same. An undefined repository variable gives an empty value.
rows.effect: `bin/ci/bench_refresh_bitfile.py` reads the bitfile identity of every FPGA card of the runner before the measurement. It stops the measurement with `bitfile mismatch` when the identity differs from this value.
rows.notes: The script also stops when the FPGA cards hold different bitfiles. That check does not need this value. The manual recipe in `doc/slice.md` reads the same name and stops when it is unset or empty.

rows.name: EXPECTED_RUNNER_CLASSES
rows.read_by: The step `Check latest scheduled refresh jobs` of the job `health` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh-health.yml`). It passes the words to `bin/ci/bench_refresh_health.py`.
rows.values: Runner class names with spaces between them. The workflow writes `2x96core 2x72core` when the repository variable `SLICE_REFRESH_2X72_ENABLED` is `true`. Otherwise it writes `2x96core`.
rows.default: Unset: does not occur. The job always defines it.
rows.effect: The health check looks at the runs of `bench-refresh.yml` from the last 14 days. It fails unless each named runner class (one kind of benchmark runner) has a measured and published refresh.
rows.notes: The step passes the value without quotes. Each word becomes one argument of `--expected-runner-classes`. A name that `bin/ci/bench_refresh_matrix.py` does not list stops the script with `unknown runner class`.

rows.name: EXPECTED_SHA7
rows.read_by: The step `Verify build content hash` of the jobs `test-host` and `test-fpga` (`.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml`)
rows.values: 7 hexadecimal characters from the job `build`. They are the start of the SHA-256 hash of the `git ls-files -s` output, without the `compile_commands.json` entries.
rows.default: Unset: the step always defines it. An empty value makes the comparison fail.
rows.effect: The step compares the value with the same hash of its own checkout. The step fails when the two differ.
rows.notes: The value is a hash of the tracked files. It is not a Git commit id.

rows.name: FEATURE_TESTING_PUBLISH
rows.read_by: `bin/ci/resolve-apt-channel.sh`
rows.values: Only the exact text `1` allows the publish. All other text refuses it. The workflow writes `0`.
rows.default: Unset: the same as `0`. The script refuses a feature-branch publish to `testing` and exits with status 1.
rows.effect: `1` lets a manual run publish a feature branch (a branch other than `main` and `release-*`) to the APT channel `testing` (a package set of the Positron APT server).
rows.notes: Tag pushes and the channel `unstable` do not need it. `main` and `release-*` branches are refused for `testing` with any value. A workflow comment says to write `1` only after the APT server keeps `~feature.` versions apart.

rows.name: GCP_NIX_JOB_TEMP_NAME
rows.read_by: Steps of 6 jobs (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`)
rows.values: Directory name without a path. The workflow writes `gcp-nix-<run id>-<run attempt>-<job id>`.
rows.default: Unset: the workflow always defines it. The cleanup step uses `${GCP_NIX_JOB_TEMP_NAME:?}`. An unset or empty value stops its `rm` command with an error.
rows.effect: It names the temporary directory of one job: `$RUNNER_TEMP/$GCP_NIX_JOB_TEMP_NAME`. The job keeps its Nix result links and other temporary files there. The last step of the job removes the directory.
rows.notes: `JOB_TEMP` holds the full path of the same directory. `bin/ci/nix-cache/test_cache.py` sets the name to `job` when it runs 3 steps of the job `tron-build`.

rows.name: GIT_SHA7
rows.read_by: The step `Run exact prebuilt benchmark` of the job `benchmark` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`). It passes the value to `bin/ci/tron-build/run_benchmark.sh` as an argument.
rows.values: Short Git commit id. An earlier step of the job writes it with `git rev-parse --short=7 HEAD`. The script keeps the first 7 characters.
rows.default: Unset: does not occur. The step always defines it.
rows.effect: `bin/ci/tron-build/run_benchmark.sh` uses it in the name of the benchmark result file: `<results directory>/<value>.<host>.json`. The results directory is `/scratch/tron-benchmark` unless `TRON_BENCHMARK_RESULTS_ROOT` is set.
rows.notes: `bin/ci/ci-run-benchmark.sh` has a script variable of the same name. That script takes the value from its second argument, not from the environment.

rows.name: HEALTH_REPORT
rows.read_by: The step `Reconcile slice refresh health issue` of the job `reconcile` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh-health.yml`). It passes the value to `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` as an argument.
rows.values: `healthy`, `stale:<platform names with commas>` or `probe-error:<error name>`. It is the output `report` of the job `health`. Other text counts as no valid report.
rows.default: Unset: the job always defines it. An empty value counts as no valid report.
rows.effect: `healthy` together with a successful job `health` closes the open GitHub issue `Slice cost-data refresh is unhealthy`. In every other case the script opens that issue or adds a comment to it.
rows.notes: The script also gets the result of the job `health` as an argument. A `stale:` or `probe-error:` report is valid only with the result `failure`. `bin/ci/bench_refresh_health.py` writes the report.

evidence.quote: diagnosis="Probe error: health job returned no valid report."

rows.name: INGEST_STORE_PATH
rows.read_by: Steps of the jobs `test-ingest` and `generate-plugins` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`). They pass it to `bin/ci/nix-cache/acquire.py`, to the ingest test scripts and to `nix build`.
rows.values: Nix store path of the ingest executable, of the form `/nix/store/<hash>-<name>`. It is the output `store_path` of the job `build-ingest`.
rows.default: Unset: does not occur. Both jobs define it.
rows.effect: The jobs fetch this store path from the Nix binary cache at `REGIONAL_NIX_CACHE`. The ingest tests run `<value>/bin/ingest`. The plugin build gets the value as the Nix argument `ingest`.

rows.name: JOB_RESULTS
rows.read_by: `bin/ci/tron-build/require_results.py`
rows.values: JSON object, parsed with `json.loads`. Each key is a job name. Each value is an object with a `result` field. The workflow writes `toJSON(needs)`.
rows.default: Unset: the script prints `'JOB_RESULTS'` and exits with status 1.
rows.effect: The script exits with status 0 only when every job has the result `success`. Otherwise it prints the jobs that did not succeed and exits with status 1.
rows.notes: Text that is not JSON and an empty object also give exit status 1. In `gcp-nix.yml` the job `test` checks the jobs `tron-build`, `test-host` and `test-fpga` this way.

evidence.quote: raise ValueError("No job results were supplied")

rows.name: JOB_TEMP
rows.who_sets: `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml` (the step `Prepare CI tools` of 5 jobs writes it to the `GITHUB_ENV` file)
rows.read_by: Later steps of the same job (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`)
rows.values: Path of a directory. The step writes `$RUNNER_TEMP/$GCP_NIX_JOB_TEMP_NAME`.
rows.default: Unset: no default. The step `Prepare CI tools` writes it before the steps that use it.
rows.effect: The steps of one job put their files below this directory: Nix result links such as `$JOB_TEMP/ingest`, the Python at `$JOB_TEMP/python/bin/python3` and the links to fetched store paths.
rows.notes: The last step of each job removes the directory. The job `test-ingest` does not set it. `bin/ci/nix-cache/test_cache.py` sets it when it runs 3 steps of the job `tron-build`.

rows.name: LAB_NIX_CACHE
rows.read_by: Workflow steps (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`, `.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`). They pass it as an option to `bin/ci/nix-cache/acquire.py` and 3 more scripts.
rows.values: URL of a Nix binary cache. Both workflows write `http://nix-store.positron.internal:5000`.
rows.default: Unset: does not occur. Both workflows define it.
rows.effect: The jobs on the FPGA runners fetch the build plan and the prebuilt test and benchmark builds of TRON from this cache. The job `wait-for-lab-cache` first waits until the cache holds the build plan.
rows.notes: No script reads the name from the environment. `bin/ci/nix-cache/test_cache.py` sets it to a `file://` address for a test.

rows.name: MACHINERY_RESULT
rows.read_by: The step `Require successful dependencies` of the job `ci-machinery-tests` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`)
rows.values: Result word of the job `ci-machinery-contracts`: `success`, `failure`, `cancelled` or `skipped`. The step compares the text with `success`.
rows.default: Unset: the step always defines it. An empty value makes the step fail.
rows.effect: The step runs `test "$MACHINERY_RESULT" = success`. The job `ci-machinery-tests` fails unless the value is `success`.
rows.notes: The same step tests `TOOLCHAIN_RESULT` in the same way. `bin/ci/test_build_test_stage.py` runs the step with each result word.

rows.name: MACHINE_CLASS
rows.read_by: The step `Run exact prebuilt benchmark` of the job `benchmark` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`). It passes the value to `bin/ci/tron-build/run_benchmark.sh` as an argument.
rows.values: Text that names the kind of benchmark runner. The job matrix writes `2x96core` or `2x72core`. The script does not check the text. Empty text is an error.
rows.default: Unset: does not occur. The step always defines it.
rows.effect: `bin/ci/tron-build/run_benchmark.sh` puts the value into the benchmark result identity (a SHA-256 hash). The identity names the cached result file. A cached result is reused only for the same machine class and host.

rows.name: MODEL_TRACE_STORE_PATH
rows.read_by: Steps of the job `generate-plugins` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`). They pass it to `bin/ci/nix-cache/acquire.py` and to `nix build`.
rows.values: Nix store path of the model traces (the files that the job `build-model-traces` exports for the test models). It is the output `store_path` of that job.
rows.default: Unset: does not occur. The job always defines it.
rows.effect: The job fetches this store path from the Nix binary cache at `REGIONAL_NIX_CACHE`. The plugin build (`nix/model-plugins-entry.nix`) gets the value as the Nix argument `modelTraces`.

rows.name: MODEL_WEIGHTS_ROOT
rows.read_by: Steps of the jobs `test-ingest` and `build-model-traces` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`). They pass it as `--weights-root` to `bin/ci/ingest/prepare_tests.py` and `bin/ci/model-traces/prepare_inputs.py`.
rows.values: Path of a directory on the runner. The workflow writes `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface`.
rows.default: Unset: does not occur. The workflow always defines it.
rows.effect: The two scripts check the Hugging Face model snapshots below this directory. They stop with an error when a snapshot is missing or has the wrong version. They do not download models.

evidence.quote: """Require one pinned snapshot without downloading or mutating it."""

rows.name: PLUGIN_STORE_PATH
rows.read_by: Steps of the job `prepare-tron-build-inputs` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`). They pass it to `bin/ci/nix-cache/acquire.py` and to `nix build`.
rows.values: Nix store path of the model plugins (the model code that ingest generates). It is the output `store_path` of the job `generate-plugins`.
rows.default: Unset: does not occur. The job always defines it.
rows.effect: The job fetches this store path from the Nix binary cache at `REGIONAL_NIX_CACHE`. The build recipe (`nix/tron-build.nix`) gets the value as the Nix argument `pluginBundle`.

rows.name: POSITRON_APT_LOGIN_TOKEN
rows.who_sets: `.github/workflows/deb-smoke.yml`, `.github/workflows/publish-deb.yml` (each copies the GitHub secret into one step)
rows.read_by: `bin/ci/ci-run-deb-package-jammy-runtime.sh`
rows.values: Secret login token for the APT server `apt.positron.internal`. The script writes the text unchanged after the word `login`.
rows.default: Unset: the script prints `FAIL: POSITRON_APT_LOGIN_TOKEN must be set` and exits with status 1. An empty value does the same.
rows.effect: The script writes the token to a temporary file. It mounts the file read-only into the Ubuntu 22.04 test container as the APT login file `/etc/apt/auth.conf.d/positron.conf`.
rows.notes: The script unsets the variable before it starts `docker`. The token is not passed as a container environment variable. Both workflows declare the secret as required for `workflow_call`.

new_terms.definition: The workflow `bench-refresh.yml`. It measures the test times and the peak memory of the Slice tests again on a benchmark runner. It then opens or updates a pull request that changes `config/test-benchmarks.json`.
The runner label that selects one kind of benchmark runner. The two classes are `2x96core` and `2x72core`.
The text `<release code>@<year>-<month>-<day>` that `bin/ci/bench_refresh_bitfile.py` builds from the release code and the release date of the bitfile in an FPGA card.
A named package set of the Positron APT server. `publish-deb.yml` publishes the `tron` Debian package to the channel `unstable` or `testing`.
For `bin/ci/resolve-apt-channel.sh`, a branch other than `main` and the `release-*` branches.
The files that the CI job `build-model-traces` exports for the test models with `bin/ci/model-traces/export.py`. The plugin build reads them with the ingest executable.
The model code that ingest generates. In CI the job `generate-plugins` builds it from the model traces.

notes: All 21 variables have a row and none is dropped. Source choices: an env entry at job level counts as 'workflow env' (DRY_RUN, ENABLE_2X72, EXPECTED_BITFILE, EXPECTED_RUNNER_CLASSES, HEALTH_REPORT, INGEST_STORE_PATH, MODEL_TRACE_STORE_PATH, PLUGIN_STORE_PATH). JOB_TEMP is 'step env': a step writes it to the GITHUB_ENV file for the later steps of the same job, and no env entry holds it. ENABLE_2X72 and EXPECTED_BITFILE take their text from repository variables with other names (SLICE_REFRESH_2X72_ENABLED, SLICE_EXPECTED_BITFILE_2X96CORE, SLICE_EXPECTED_BITFILE_2X72CORE). Correction of the collected facts: they said that a DRY_RUN dry run 'opens no pull request'. The job 'publish' decides that from the workflow input dry_run (bench-refresh.yml:253), not from the DRY_RUN variable. The row says so. The collected facts for EXPECTED_BITFILE had confidence 'medium'. The code confirms them and adds one fact: an empty value disables only the identity comparison (bench_refresh_bitfile.py:155). GIT_SHA7: bin/ci/ci-run-benchmark.sh assigns a script variable of the same name from its second argument and never reads the environment value. Evidence quotes are the source line without its indentation. Four quotes are an exact part of the line, not the whole line: bench-refresh-health.yml:44 holds a pipe character, and gcp-nix.yml:390 (2 quotes) and gcp-nix.yml:432 are longer than 120 characters. Six whole-line quotes end with a shell line-continuation backslash. bench-refresh.yml:58, the DRY_RUN entry of the job 'plan', is not quoted: it holds a pipe character. Statements that a variable 'does not occur' unset rest on the env entry of the workflow, which always defines the name. The 4 result words of MACHINERY_RESULT are the GitHub Actions job results. bin/ci/test_build_test_stage.py:1656 lists the 3 unsuccessful ones.
